- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to account for mean reversion — reduce forecast peak by 1–2% and smooth subsequent days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.15) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate future prices — apply a mild downward bias (–0.5 to –1.5%) to avoid overconfidence.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early days of a 30-day forecast — especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast values.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.17 to -0.61 in 3–5 days), model often misjudges direction — align forecast with sentiment trend shift, not just historical mean.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in long-term (30d) forecasts — incorporate sentiment variance as a multiplier (e.g., +0.2–0.5% per 0.1 sentiment deviation) to adjust for uncertainty.
